business: A manufacturer of consumer packaged goods. It buys materials, makes and tests product, and releases it for despatch, through its own factories and through outside manufacturers.
in_scope: Buying materials, and deciding which suppliers may supply them
Defining products — what they are made from and what they must be
Defining how products are made — the steps, the settings and the recipes
The layout of each factory and the machines in it
Making product, and what each batch actually used and produced
Testing, recording problems, putting them right, and releasing product
Tracing any batch back to its ingredients and forward to where it went
Stock held at the organisation's own sites
Product made or packed by outside manufacturers
out_of_scope: Trade spending, promotions and pricing with retailers
What happens on the shelf in store
Market share and sales data bought from research firms
Research and development before a product is formally defined
assumptions: The factory, laboratory, quality and maintenance systems already in place stay in place. This model holds what they record; it does not replace them.
Material held by a supplier or outside manufacturer is theirs. It becomes the organisation's on receipt, and the organisation holds no stock at any party it does not operate.
Something bought as an ingredient or part may be another company's finished product. What it is made from is theirs and may not be known here.
This is research-only work. No business owner has reviewed the requirements.
questions_unanswered: Is finished output identified individually, or only by batch?
The model supports both, so nothing here assumes either — but whether individual units are tracked changes how much of it is used.
What proportion of output is made by outside manufacturers?
Where it is most of it, the organisation holds little production record of its own, and the model is mainly about what partners must supply.
